244		} else {

16	// sourceDetailLevelingDBNotFound es el detalle de fuente estampado en el
17	// envelope de "no encontrado" del PATCH (el repo devuelve un `nil` a secas
18	// ahí, así que el handler no tiene un `Sourced` del que leerlo). Se
19	// mantiene en paralelo con `mongo.SourceDetailModuleLevelingDB` — el
20	// handler no puede importar el paquete de infraestructura mongo sin violar
21	// las capas, así que el string se duplica localmente. Mismo patrón que
22	// `sourceDetailTicketsDBNotFound`.
23	const sourceDetailLevelingDBNotFound = "mongo.guild.module_leveling"

25	// ModuleLevelingHandler cablea los dos endpoints de niveles (GET/PATCH
26	// scoped a guild) tras un único struct. Espeja al handler de tickets:
27	// payload `*dbguild.ModuleLeveling` para que los caminos "no encontrado"
28	// emitan `"data":null`, sin pre-chequeo de guild (una guild ausente da
29	// MODULE_NOT_FOUND, no GUILD_NOT_FOUND).
30	type ModuleLevelingHandler struct {
31		Repo mongorepo.ModuleLevelingRepo
32	}
33	
34	// NewModuleLevelingHandler construye el handler.
35	func NewModuleLevelingHandler(repo mongorepo.ModuleLevelingRepo) *ModuleLevelingHandler {
36		return &ModuleLevelingHandler{Repo: repo}
37	}
38	
39	// Get devuelve el subdocumento de niveles completo (con defaults y
40	// normalizado) con las cabeceras de fuente estampadas, o un 400
41	// MODULE_NOT_FOUND con `data:null` + fuente cuando la guild todavía no
42	// tiene config de niveles.
43	func (h *ModuleLevelingHandler) Get(c fiber.Ctx) error {
44		r := result.New[*dbguild.ModuleLeveling]()
45		ctx := c.Context()
46	
47		sourced, err := h.Repo.FindModule(ctx, c.Params("bot_id"), c.Params("guild_id"))
48		if err != nil {
49			r.AddError(apierrors.New(apierrors.Props{
50				Message:    err.Error(),
51				Type:       apierrors.TypeInternal,
52				Context:    apierrors.ContextSystem,
53				StatusCode: 500,
54			}))
55			return reply(c, r)
56		}
57		if sourced != nil {
58			r.SetSource(result.Source(sourced.Source), sourced.SourceDetail)
59		}
60		if sourced == nil || sourced.Data.SchemaVersion == 0 {
61			r.SetData(nil)
62			r.AddError(apierrors.MongoMessage("Module not found", apierrors.CodeModuleNotFound))
63			return reply(c, r)
64		}
65		d := sourced.Data
66		r.SetData(&d)
67		return reply(c, r)
68	}
69	
70	// Patch valida el body estricto (`DisallowUnknownFields`), lo redecodifica
71	// como `map[string]any` para que la PRESENCIA de claves sobreviva, y el
72	// repo lo mezcla con `MergeDeepJSON` sobre el subdocumento actual. Un body
73	// vacío `{}` es un no-op que igualmente bumpea `schema_version`. Una guild
74	// ausente → 400 MODULE_NOT_FOUND con `data:null`.
75	func (h *ModuleLevelingHandler) Patch(c fiber.Ctx) error {
76		r := result.New[*dbguild.ModuleLeveling]()
77		ctx := c.Context()
78	
79		var body validations.UpdateModuleLevelingBody
80		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(c.Body()))
81		dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
82		if err := dec.Decode(&body); err != nil {
83			r.AddError(apierrors.New(apierrors.Props{
84				Message:    err.Error(),
85				Type:       apierrors.TypeValidation,
86				Context:    apierrors.ContextAPI,
87				StatusCode: 400,
88			}))
89			return reply(c, r)
90		}
91	
92		patch, err := patchMap(c.Body())
93		if err != nil {
94			r.AddError(apierrors.New(apierrors.Props{
95				Message:    err.Error(),
96				Type:       apierrors.TypeValidation,
97				Context:    apierrors.ContextAPI,
98				StatusCode: 400,
99			}))
100			return reply(c, r)
101		}
102	
103		sourced, err := h.Repo.Update(ctx, c.Params("bot_id"), c.Params("guild_id"), patch)
104		if err != nil {
105			r.AddError(apierrors.New(apierrors.Props{
106				Message:    err.Error(),
107				Type:       apierrors.TypeInternal,
108				Context:    apierrors.ContextSystem,
109				StatusCode: 500,
110			}))
111			return reply(c, r)
112		}
113		if sourced == nil || sourced.Data.SchemaVersion == 0 {
114			r.SetSource(result.SourceDB, sourceDetailLevelingDBNotFound)
115			r.SetData(nil)
116			r.AddError(apierrors.MongoMessage("Module not found", apierrors.CodeModuleNotFound))
117			return reply(c, r)
118		}
119		d := sourced.Data
120		r.SetData(&d)
121		r.SetSource(result.Source(sourced.Source), sourced.SourceDetail)
122		return reply(c, r)
123	}

7	// UpdateModuleTempvoiceBody mirrors the Node `updateModuleTempVoiceSchema` (a
8	// `.strict()` object of `.optional()` fields). Unlike the READ schema, the
9	// PATCH schema excludes only `schema_version` and `updated_at` (server-managed).
10	// The top-level `name_blacklist`, `panel` and `command_mode` (added in v3/v4/v7)
11	// ARE patchable — omitting them here made the strict decoder reject them as
12	// `unrecognized_keys` on any PATCH that included them (e.g. saving the panel from
13	// the dashboard) → 400. Every field is a pointer so the strict decoder can validate
14	// the shape; the handler then re-decodes the SAME raw body as `map[string]any`,
15	// which the repository merges into the existing subdoc via
16	// `mongo.MergeDeepJSON` by KEY PRESENCE: a key absent in the body is left
17	// alone; an explicit `false`/`0`/`""`/`null` is applied and overrides the
18	// stored value; nested objects recurse (so a partial
19	// `{"defaults":{"bitrate":96000}}` PATCH preserves the other defaults);
20	// slices (`creators`) replace wholesale; maps merge per-key.
21	//
22	// PER OLA-3 NOTE: the greeter/logs/music bodies bind via Fiber's default
23	// decoder (silently drops unknown keys, parity with Mongoose) — only
24	// modmail/tempvoice/giveaway/moderation carry the strict unknown-key
25	// rejection. The nested field types are the full `dbguild.Tempvoice*`
26	// shapes: every zod PATCH sub-schema matches its parent type
27	// field-for-field, so no valid key is rejected. Go's json decoder does
28	// NOT enforce zod's REQUIRED-ness inside a present nested object, so a
29	// partial command entry that Node would 400 is accepted here and the
30	// missing leaves stay zero — the same non-strict-required behaviour
31	// every Go module body has.
32	type UpdateModuleTempvoiceBody struct {
33		Enabled        *bool                                `json:"enabled,omitempty"`
34		Creators       *[]dbguild.TempvoiceCreator          `json:"creators,omitempty"`
35		NameBlacklist  *[]string                            `json:"name_blacklist,omitempty"`
36		Panel          *dbguild.TempvoicePanel              `json:"panel,omitempty"`
37		CommandMode    *dbguild.TempvoiceCommandMode        `json:"command_mode,omitempty"`
38		Defaults       *dbguild.TempvoiceDefaults           `json:"defaults,omitempty"`
39		CommandsGlobal *dbguild.TempvoiceCommandAccess      `json:"commands_global,omitempty"`
40		Commands       *map[string]dbguild.TempvoiceCommand `json:"commands,omitempty"`
41	}

14	// Request DTOs + parsers para las seis rutas `/leveling/bots/:bot_id/guilds/:guild_id/**`
15	// (§8 del contrato). Vertical NUEVA sin contraparte en el Node api-db, así
16	// que no hay un zod que mirrorear byte a byte — pero, a diferencia del resto
17	// del paquete (moderation_flow_runs_validations.go, etc.), esta vertical
18	// NUNCA responde 400 por un `scope`, `curve_multiplier`, delta de XP,
19	// `limit` u `offset` ausente o mal formado: el propio contrato lo pide
20	// explícito para curve_multiplier ("si falta o no es válido, default 1") y
21	// aquí se aplica el MISMO criterio a los otros cuatro, porque los cinco son
22	// parámetros de LECTURA/ESCRITURA DERIVADA (§3), no validaciones de
23	// negocio — el repositorio ya clampa limit/offset a sus rangos (ver
24	// LevelingRepository.Top). El único 400 real de esta vertical es
25	// `user_id` ausente dentro de una entrada de `POST /xp/bulk` (no tiene
26	// default razonable) o un body que ni siquiera es JSON válido.
27	//
28	// Reusa los helpers compartidos del paquete: parseRequiredString,
29	// bodyBindError, isJSONNull (definidos en otros ficheros de este mismo
30	// paquete).
31	
32	// levelingDefaultTopLimit es el default de `limit` en GET .../top cuando el
33	// query param falta o no es numérico — no lo fija el contrato, pero es el
34	// tamaño habitual de un leaderboard "top". El repositorio clampa el valor
35	// final (venga de aquí o del cliente) a [1,100].
36	const levelingDefaultTopLimit = 10
37	
38	// parseLevelingInt intenta leer `raw` como entero; ausente o no numérico →
39	// `def`. Sin validación estricta a propósito (ver el comentario de
40	// package): limit/offset son parámetros de lectura derivada y el
41	// repositorio ya los clampa a su rango válido.
42	func parseLevelingInt(raw string, def int) int {
43		if raw == "" {
44			return def
45		}
46		v, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
47		if err != nil {
48			return def
49		}
50		return v
51	}
52	
53	// parseLevelingCurveMultiplier interpreta el query param `curve_multiplier`:
54	// ausente, no numérico, no-positivo, NaN o infinito → 1 (el default de
55	// DBModuleLeveling — §8: "si falta o no es válido, default 1"). Nunca
56	// produce un 400.
57	func parseLevelingCurveMultiplier(raw string) float64 {
58		if raw == "" {
59			return 1
60		}
61		v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(raw), 64)
62		if err != nil || v <= 0 || math.IsNaN(v) || math.IsInf(v, 0) {
63			return 1
64		}
65		return v
66	}
67	
68	// parseLevelingCurveMultiplierBody es el equivalente de
69	// parseLevelingCurveMultiplier para el campo `curve_multiplier` del body
70	// (POST /users/:user_id/xp y POST /xp/bulk) — mismo default, mismas
71	// condiciones de invalidez.
72	func parseLevelingCurveMultiplierBody(raw json.RawMessage) float64 {
73		if raw == nil || isJSONNull(raw) {
74			return 1
75		}
76		var v float64
77		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &v); err != nil || v <= 0 || math.IsNaN(v) || math.IsInf(v, 0) {
78			return 1
79		}
80		return v
81	}
82	
83	// parseLevelingNonNegInt64 interpreta un delta de XP del body (text_xp,
84	// voice_xp, messages, voice_seconds): ausente o null → 0; negativo o de
85	// otro tipo → 0 (clampeado, nunca 400 — ver el comentario de package); si
86	// no, el entero (truncado si llega con decimales).
87	func parseLevelingNonNegInt64(raw json.RawMessage) int64 {
88		if raw == nil || isJSONNull(raw) {
89			return 0
90		}
91		var v float64
92		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &v); err != nil || v < 0 {
93			return 0
94		}
95		return int64(v)
96	}
97	
98	// parseLevelingBool interpreta `touch_message`: ausente, null o cualquier
99	// valor no-booleano → false.
100	func parseLevelingBool(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
101		if raw == nil || isJSONNull(raw) {
102			return false
103		}
104		var b bool
105		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &b); err != nil {
106			return false
107		}
108		return b
109	}

111	// ─── GET /leveling/bots/:bot_id/guilds/:guild_id/top ──────────────────────
112	
113	// ParseLevelingTopQuery mirrors la query de GET .../top: `scope` (default
114	// "unified" — dbleveling.NormalizeScope), `curve_multiplier` (default 1),
115	// `limit` (default levelingDefaultTopLimit, el repositorio clampa a
116	// [1,100]), `offset` (default 0, el repositorio clampa a >=0).
117	func ParseLevelingTopQuery(scope, curveMultiplierRaw, limitRaw, offsetRaw string) (normScope string, curveMultiplier float64, limit, offset int) {
118		return dbleveling.NormalizeScope(scope),
119			parseLevelingCurveMultiplier(curveMultiplierRaw),
120			parseLevelingInt(limitRaw, levelingDefaultTopLimit),
121			parseLevelingInt(offsetRaw, 0)
122	}
123	
124	// ─── GET /leveling/bots/:bot_id/guilds/:guild_id/users/:user_id ───────────
125	
126	// ParseLevelingUserQuery mirrors la query de GET .../users/:user_id:
127	// `scope` (default "unified"), `curve_multiplier` (default 1).
128	func ParseLevelingUserQuery(scope, curveMultiplierRaw string) (normScope string, curveMultiplier float64) {
129		return dbleveling.NormalizeScope(scope), parseLevelingCurveMultiplier(curveMultiplierRaw)
130	}
131	
132	// ─── POST /leveling/bots/:bot_id/guilds/:guild_id/users/:user_id/xp ───────
133	
134	// ParseLevelingAddXP mirrors el body de POST .../users/:user_id/xp:
135	// `{text_xp?, voice_xp?, messages?, voice_seconds?, curve_multiplier?,
136	// touch_message?}` — TODOS opcionales. Un body vacío (`{}`, `null`, o
137	// ausente) es válido: los cuatro deltas quedan a 0, que es el "touch" del
138	// §3 (re-deriva y persiste los niveles de este miembro sin conceder XP).
139	// El único error posible es un body que ni siquiera es JSON válido.
140	func ParseLevelingAddXP(body []byte) (dbleveling.AddXPInput, *apierrors.CustomError) {
141		var raw struct {
142			TextXP          json.RawMessage `json:"text_xp"`
143			VoiceXP         json.RawMessage `json:"voice_xp"`
144			Messages        json.RawMessage `json:"messages"`
145			VoiceSeconds    json.RawMessage `json:"voice_seconds"`
146			CurveMultiplier json.RawMessage `json:"curve_multiplier"`
147			TouchMessage    json.RawMessage `json:"touch_message"`
148		}
149		if len(body) > 0 {
150			if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &raw); err != nil {
151				return dbleveling.AddXPInput{}, bodyBindError(err)
152			}
153		}
154		return dbleveling.AddXPInput{
155			TextXP:          parseLevelingNonNegInt64(raw.TextXP),
156			VoiceXP:         parseLevelingNonNegInt64(raw.VoiceXP),
157			Messages:        parseLevelingNonNegInt64(raw.Messages),
158			VoiceSeconds:    parseLevelingNonNegInt64(raw.VoiceSeconds),
159			CurveMultiplier: parseLevelingCurveMultiplierBody(raw.CurveMultiplier),
160			TouchMessage:    parseLevelingBool(raw.TouchMessage),
161		}, nil
162	}
163	
164	// ─── POST /leveling/bots/:bot_id/guilds/:guild_id/xp/bulk ─────────────────
165	
166	// ParseLevelingAddXPBulk mirrors el body de POST .../xp/bulk:
167	// `{entries: [{user_id, text_xp?, voice_xp?, messages?, voice_seconds?,
168	// touch_message?}], curve_multiplier?}`. `user_id` es el ÚNICO campo
169	// REQUERIDO de todo este endpoint — dentro de cada entrada, no tiene un
170	// default razonable — y falla con el índice exacto en la property
171	// (`entries.N.user_id`) para señalar la fila. `entries` ausente o vacío es
172	// válido: el repositorio lo trata como no-op. `curve_multiplier` es
173	// COMPARTIDO por todo el lote (§8), no por entrada.
174	func ParseLevelingAddXPBulk(body []byte) ([]dbleveling.BulkEntry, float64, *apierrors.CustomError) {
175		var raw struct {
176			Entries []struct {
177				UserID       json.RawMessage `json:"user_id"`
178				TextXP       json.RawMessage `json:"text_xp"`
179				VoiceXP      json.RawMessage `json:"voice_xp"`
180				Messages     json.RawMessage `json:"messages"`
181				VoiceSeconds json.RawMessage `json:"voice_seconds"`
182				TouchMessage json.RawMessage `json:"touch_message"`
183			} `json:"entries"`
184			CurveMultiplier json.RawMessage `json:"curve_multiplier"`
185		}
186		if len(body) > 0 {
187			if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &raw); err != nil {
188				return nil, 1, bodyBindError(err)
189			}
190		}
191	
192		entries := make([]dbleveling.BulkEntry, 0, len(raw.Entries))
193		for i, e := range raw.Entries {
194			userID, verr := parseRequiredString(e.UserID, fmt.Sprintf("entries.%d.user_id", i), 1, 32)
195			if verr != nil {
196				return nil, 1, verr
197			}
198			entries = append(entries, dbleveling.BulkEntry{
199				UserID:       userID,
200				TextXP:       parseLevelingNonNegInt64(e.TextXP),
201				VoiceXP:      parseLevelingNonNegInt64(e.VoiceXP),
202				Messages:     parseLevelingNonNegInt64(e.Messages),
203				VoiceSeconds: parseLevelingNonNegInt64(e.VoiceSeconds),
204				TouchMessage: parseLevelingBool(e.TouchMessage),
205			})
206		}
207		return entries, parseLevelingCurveMultiplierBody(raw.CurveMultiplier), nil
208	}

19	// TTL: every SetModule call applies `ModuleTTLSeconds` when ttlSeconds is
20	// zero/unset. The TTL is a BACKSTOP, not the invalidation mechanism: every
21	// `Update` on a module repo is write-through and every delete invalidates
22	// explicitly, so a correct system never needs the timer. It exists only to
23	// bound the damage of a *missed* invalidation (a Redis blip that swallowed a
24	// DEL, a schema bump that left an unreadable hash) — the same reasoning as
25	// the `botsListTTLSeconds` backstop in bot_cache.go.
26	//
27	// It used to be 1 hour, which made the backstop the dominant cost of the
28	// whole service: every guild with any activity re-read its modules from
29	// Mongo once an hour whether or not anything had changed. See
30	// ANALISIS-CACHE.md — that single constant accounted for most of the
31	// ~30M monthly DB ops.
32	//
33	// The cache only stores the module subdoc (the `module_music` block of
34	// the guild doc), not the entire guild. This means module PATCHes do
35	// not invalidate the wider guild cache, but reading requires either a
36	// cache hit here or a fresh Mongo projection — which `ModuleRepository`
37	// handles.
38	type ModuleCache struct {
39		client *Client
40	}

42	// ModuleTTLSeconds is the backstop TTL applied to module cache writes and to
43	// the `enabled_modules` snapshot. 24h, not 1h: at 1h the timer was firing
44	// ~24x more often than any real invalidation needed it to, and each firing
45	// cost a Mongo read per active guild.
46	//
47	// Not TTL-less (unlike the guild hash in guild_cache.go) on purpose: a missed
48	// invalidation on a module would leave a guild's module config wrong until
49	// something wrote to it again, which for a rarely-edited module means
50	// "forever". 24h bounds that at one day while removing 96% of the refreshes.
51	const ModuleTTLSeconds = 86400

67	// enabledModulesSnapshotKey holds the cached answer to "which modules does this
68	// guild have enabled" as a JSON array — including the empty array.

70	// It exists because a Redis SET cannot be empty: SADD-ing zero members leaves
71	// no key, so in the SET alone "this guild has 0 enabled modules" and "we have
72	// never computed this guild's modules" are the same observable state. That
73	// ambiguity was not a corner case — a guild that added the bot and never ran
74	// `/config` is the most common guild there is, so the ambiguous branch was the
75	// hot branch, and every one of those guilds re-derived its empty module list
76	// from Mongo on a timer, forever.
77	//
78	// The answer lives in this ONE key rather than in a boolean marker beside the
79	// SET on purpose. Two keys with independent expiry can be observed
80	// half-expired: if the SET went first, a surviving marker would assert "no
81	// modules enabled" for a guild that has some. Reading a single key cannot
82	// produce that. The SET is still written for external consumers (dashboards,
83	// the music picker) that read `enabled_modules` directly, but it is no longer
84	// what `GetEnabledModules` trusts.

86		return fmt.Sprintf("bots:%s:guilds:%s:enabled_modules_cached", botID, guildID)
87	}

94	// GetModule returns the deserialized module subdoc, or nil when missing.
95	// The returned map is the raw hash with each value deserialized via
96	// `DeserializeValue` (booleans, numbers, dates, JSON objects). The caller
97	// is responsible for unmarshalling into the typed `dbguild.ModuleMusic`
98	// (or greeter/logs) shape.
99	func (m *ModuleCache) GetModule(ctx context.Context, botID, guildID, moduleKey string) (map[string]any, error) {
100		raw, err := m.client.HGetAll(ctx, m.moduleKey(botID, guildID, moduleKey))
101		if err != nil || raw == nil {
102			return nil, err
103		}
104		out := make(map[string]any, len(raw))
105		for k, v := range raw {
106			out[k] = DeserializeValue(v)
107		}
108		return out, nil
109	}

111	// SetModule writes the module subdoc with TTL=ModuleTTLSeconds by default
112	// (override via `ttlSeconds > 0`). The write is best-effort: a Redis
113	// failure is logged and swallowed so the caller can still return a
114	// successful response (the Mongo write already succeeded).
115	//
116	// The three Redis commands (DEL + HSET + EXPIRE) are pipelined in a
117	// single round-trip so the cache key never lands in an intermediate
118	// "fields from the previous schema_version, no TTL" state that a racing
119	// reader could observe. The DEL is the important part: without it the
120	// hash could carry stale fields from a prior schema bump indefinitely.
121	// The pipelined EXPIRE is the second important part: HSET on an existing
122	// key with no TTL is a no-op for the timer, so we have to (re-)arm the
123	// TTL atomically with the HSET — sequential HSET-then-EXPIRE would
124	// leave the key TTL-less if the second call failed.
125	//
126	// Side effects on the enabled SET are intentionally NOT performed here —
127	// the Node `setModule` clears the `enabled_modules_checked` tombstone but
128	// only the Node setModule variant (called from internal repo paths) does
129	// the SADD/SREM gymnastics. The Go port mirrors the simpler behaviour:
130	// just the module hash + TTL. The `enabled_modules` SET itself is
131	// maintained by `EnabledHandler.listEnabled` (see `SetEnabledModules`).
132	func (m *ModuleCache) SetModule(ctx context.Context, botID, guildID, moduleKey string, fields map[string]string, ttlSeconds int) error {
133		if ttlSeconds <= 0 {
134			ttlSeconds = ModuleTTLSeconds
135		}
136		if len(fields) == 0 {
137			return nil
138		}
139		key := m.moduleKey(botID, guildID, moduleKey)
140		resps := m.client.DoMulti(ctx,
141			m.client.DelPipeline(key),
142			m.client.HSetPipeline(key, fields),
143			m.client.ExpirePipeline(key, ttlSeconds),
144		)
145		// All three commands must succeed for the write to be considered
146		// committed. DEL is idempotent (returns 0 on missing key) so a non-
147		// nil error there is a real network failure.
148		for i, r := range resps {
149			if err := r.Error(); err != nil {
150				return fmt.Errorf("module cache pipeline step %d: %w", i, err)
151			}
152		}
153		return nil
154	}

163	// GetEnabledModules reads the cached snapshot of enabled module keys.
164	//
165	// The second return value is what makes this usable as a cache: it reports
166	// whether a snapshot EXISTS, independently of whether it is empty. `([], true,
167	// nil)` means "we computed this guild and it has no modules enabled" — a hit,
168	// answerable without Mongo. `(nil, false, nil)` means "never computed" and is
169	// the only case the caller must resolve against the database.
170	//
171	// A snapshot that fails to decode is reported as a miss rather than an error:
172	// the only cost is one resolve, which then overwrites the bad value. Same
173	// posture as the module hashes, which fall through to Mongo when their fields
174	// cannot be parsed.
175	func (m *ModuleCache) GetEnabledModules(ctx context.Context, botID, guildID string) ([]string, bool, error) {
176		raw, found, err := m.client.Get(ctx, m.enabledModulesSnapshotKey(botID, guildID))
177		if err != nil {
178			return nil, false, err
179		}
180		if !found {
181			return nil, false, nil
182		}
183		var keys []string
184		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &keys); err != nil {
185			return nil, false, nil
186		}
187		if keys == nil {
188			keys = []string{}
189		}
190		return keys, true, nil
191	}

193	// SetEnabledModules writes both representations of the enabled-module snapshot:
194	// the JSON key `GetEnabledModules` reads, and the `enabled_modules` SET that
195	// external consumers (dashboards, the music picker) read directly.
196	//
197	// SET members are flat strings (`music`, `greeter`, `logs`) and both keys carry
198	// `ModuleTTLSeconds`, matching the per-module HASHes.
199	//
200	// An empty `keys` slice is NOT a no-op any more: it DELs the SET and writes an
201	// empty JSON array, which is how "this guild has no modules enabled" gets
202	// cached. That used to be skipped entirely, leaving the most common guild shape
203	// permanently uncacheable (see `enabledModulesSnapshotKey`).
204	//
205	// Single pipeline so the two representations cannot disagree for longer than a
206	// round-trip, and DEL-before-SADD so a shrinking module list drops members
207	// instead of accumulating them.
208	//
209	// Called from `EnabledHandler.listEnabled` once it has resolved the enabled
210	// keys. Best-effort: a Redis failure is returned to the caller, which logs it
211	// and still answers the request (the data in the response is already correct).
212	func (m *ModuleCache) SetEnabledModules(ctx context.Context, botID, guildID string, keys []string) error {
213		setKey := m.enabledModulesKey(botID, guildID)
214		snapshotKey := m.enabledModulesSnapshotKey(botID, guildID)
215	
216		if keys == nil {
217			keys = []string{}
218		}
219		encoded, err := json.Marshal(keys)
220		if err != nil {
221			return fmt.Errorf("marshal enabled_modules snapshot: %w", err)
222		}
223	
224		cmds := []rueidis.Completed{m.client.DelPipeline(setKey)}
225		if len(keys) > 0 {
226			cmds = append(cmds,
227				m.client.SAddPipeline(setKey, keys...),
228				m.client.ExpirePipeline(setKey, ModuleTTLSeconds),
229			)
230		}
231		cmds = append(cmds, m.client.SetExPipeline(snapshotKey, string(encoded), ModuleTTLSeconds))
232	
233		for i, r := range m.client.DoMulti(ctx, cmds...) {
234			if err := r.Error(); err != nil {
235				return fmt.Errorf("enabled_modules pipeline step %d: %w", i, err)
236			}
237		}
238		return nil
239	}

241	// DeleteEnabledSet removes both the enabled_modules SET and the JSON snapshot.
242	// Used when a guild is deleted (`bots_guilds_handler.Delete`), and by every
243	// module write via `invalidateEnabledSnapshot`.

245	// Both keys must go: leaving the snapshot behind would keep serving a stale
246	// answer — which, right after a module was enabled or disabled, is exactly the

248	func (m *ModuleCache) DeleteEnabledSet(ctx context.Context, botID, guildID string) error {

294	// MarshalModuleGreeter serializes a typed `dbguild.ModuleGreeter` subdoc.
295	// Mirrors MarshalModuleMusic but for the greeter block.
296	//
297	// Nested objects (`welcome`, `goodbye`, `captcha`, `join_roles`,
298	// `variables`) are JSON-encoded; the `updated_at` date uses the
299	// `__DATE__:` prefix so the round-trip is lossless.
300	//
301	// The captcha block is optional — encoded as JSON-null when nil so the
302	// cache stays byte-compatible with the Node service which always emits
303	// the captcha subdoc (or absent in older migrations).
304	func MarshalModuleGreeter(m dbguild.ModuleGreeter) (map[string]string, error) {
305		out := map[string]string{}
306		out["schema_version"] = SerializeValue(m.SchemaVersion)
307		out["enabled"] = SerializeValue(m.Enabled)
308		// `enabled_since` nullable: `__DATE__:<ISO>` cuando hay fecha, cadena
309		// vacía cuando no — DeserializeValue("") devuelve nil, que decodifica
310		// al puntero nil del struct (misma convención que nullableStringField).
311		if m.EnabledSince != nil {
312			out["enabled_since"] = dateField(m.EnabledSince.Time)
313		} else {
314			out["enabled_since"] = ""
315		}
316		putJSONInline(out, "welcome", m.Welcome)
317		putJSONInline(out, "goodbye", m.Goodbye)
318		putJSONInline(out, "boost", m.Boost)
319		// ⚠️ Esta función es una lista de campos A MANO: lo que no se escriba aquí
320		// NO se cachea, y como la caché se reescribe en cada PATCH y se sirve
321		// mientras `schema_version` cuadre, el campo olvidado vuelve a su valor
322		// cero en la siguiente lectura — se guarda en Mongo y "no se guarda" para
323		// el usuario. Le pasó a `boost_reaction` recién nacido en v15. Si añades
324		// un campo a `ModuleGreeter`, añádelo también aquí.
325		putJSONInline(out, "boost_reaction", m.BoostReaction)
326		putJSONInline(out, "join_roles", m.JoinRoles)
327		// Captcha nullable: misma convención que `enabled_since` — cadena vacía
328		// cuando no hay bloque. NO vale escribir la cadena "null": ni el
329		// DeserializeValue de Go ni el de Node (RedisCacheClient.deserializeValue)
330		// tienen un caso para ella, así que ambos la devolverían como el *string*
331		// "null" y el bson.Unmarshal de mapToModuleGreeter abortaría entero con
332		// "cannot decode string into a dbguild.GreeterCaptcha". FindModule
333		// reaccionaría borrando la caché y releyendo Mongo, que reescribiría el
334		// mismo valor: cache-miss permanente para ese guild.
335		if m.Captcha != nil {
336			putJSONInline(out, "captcha", *m.Captcha)
337		} else {
338			out["captcha"] = ""
339		}
340		putJSONInline(out, "variables", m.Variables)
341		out["updated_at"] = dateField(m.UpdatedAt.Time)
342		return out, nil
343	}

345	// putJSONInline is a marshaller-local variant of the package-private
346	// `putJSON` (defined in guild_cache.go). The greeter marshaller uses
347	// the inline form because the greeter marshaller signature returns
348	// `(map[string]string, error)` for consistency with the music
349	// marshaller, while the guild marshaller returns the same. To avoid
350	// breaking the existing `putJSON` contract (which propagates errors),
351	// the greeter path uses a fire-and-forget variant that writes a
352	// `__MARSHAL_ERR__:...` sentinel on failure. The next cache read will
353	// see the malformed field and fall back to Mongo, which is the same
354	// behavior the music marshaller follows.
355	func putJSONInline(out map[string]string, key string, v any) {
356		b, err := json.Marshal(v)
357		if err != nil {
358			out[key] = fmt.Sprintf("__MARSHAL_ERR__:%v", err)
359			return
360		}
361		out[key] = string(b)
362	}

364	// dateField encodes a `time.Time` as `__DATE__:<ISO>` — same form the
365	// generic `SerializeValue` uses but exposed here so the greeter
366	// marshaller doesn't have to import dbguild's JSONDate just to call it.
367	func dateField(t time.Time) string {
368		return "__DATE__:" + t.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05.000Z")
369	}

676	// nullableStringField encodes a `*string` the way the Node cache writer's
677	// `serializeValue` does: nil → "" (empty field), else the raw string as-is.
678	// On read, DeserializeValue("") → nil, round-tripping back to a nil pointer.
679	func nullableStringField(p *string) string {
680		if p == nil {
681			return ""
682		}
683		return *p
684	}

686	// nullableIntField — el gemelo de `nullableStringField` para `*int`: nil → ""
687	// (DeserializeValue("") = nil → puntero nil al decodificar el hash), número →
688	// su forma serializada normal.
689	func nullableIntField(p *int) string {
690		if p == nil {
691			return ""
692		}
693		return SerializeValue(*p)
694	}

696	// nullableDateField encodes el `enabled_since` opcional con la misma
697	// convención que el resto de nulos del hash: `__DATE__:<ISO>` cuando hay
698	// fecha, cadena vacía cuando no — `DeserializeValue("")` devuelve nil, que
699	// decodifica al puntero nil del struct. Evita repetir el if/else en los ocho
700	// marshallers.
701	func nullableDateField(d *dbguild.JSONDate) string {
702		if d == nil {
703			return ""
704		}
705		return dateField(d.Time)
706	}

69	func (r *ModuleLevelingRepository) FindModule(ctx context.Context, botID, guildID string) (*Sourced[dbguild.ModuleLeveling], error) {
70		// Camino rápido de caché.
71		if cached, err := r.cache.GetModule(ctx, botID, guildID, "leveling"); err == nil && cached != nil {
72			var m dbguild.ModuleLeveling
73			if err := mapToModuleLeveling(cached, &m); err == nil && m.SchemaVersion != 0 {
74				dbguild.NormalizeLeveling(&m)
75				return &Sourced[dbguild.ModuleLeveling]{
76					Data:         m,
77					Source:       "cache",
78					SourceDetail: SourceDetailModuleLevelingCache,
79				}, nil
80			}
81			// Fallo de parseo o schema desactualizado → se descarta y se relee.
82			_ = r.cache.DeleteModule(ctx, botID, guildID, "leveling")
83		}
84	
85		// Camino lento: proyecta sólo el bloque module_leveling.
86		filter := bson.M{"bot_id": botID, "guild_id": guildID}
87		projection := bson.M{"module_leveling": 1}
88		var out struct {
89			ModuleLeveling dbguild.ModuleLeveling `bson:"module_leveling"`
90		}
91		if err := r.coll.FindOne(ctx, filter, options.FindOne().SetProjection(projection)).Decode(&out); err != nil {
92			if stderrors.Is(err, mongo.ErrNoDocuments) {
93				return &Sourced[dbguild.ModuleLeveling]{
94					Data:         dbguild.ModuleLeveling{},
95					Source:       "db",
96					SourceDetail: SourceDetailModuleLevelingDB,
97				}, nil
98			}
99			return nil, err
100		}

102		m := out.ModuleLeveling
103		if m.SchemaVersion == 0 {
104			m = mocks.NewModuleLeveling()
105		}
106		dbguild.NormalizeLeveling(&m)
107	
108		if fields, err := redis.MarshalModuleLeveling(m); err == nil {
109			_ = r.cache.SetModule(ctx, botID, guildID, "leveling", fields, redis.ModuleTTLSeconds)
110		}
111	
112		return &Sourced[dbguild.ModuleLeveling]{

120	// `MergeDeepJSON` (recursivo, basado en presencia): un body con `text.min`

123	// un `false`/`0`/`null` explícito SE APLICA. Sólo se bumpea `updatedAt` a
124	// nivel de guild vía `$currentDate`. Una guild inexistente devuelve `nil`
125	// (el handler lo traduce a 400 MODULE_NOT_FOUND). Serializado por guild.

128		defer unlock()

131		var before struct {
132			ModuleLeveling dbguild.ModuleLeveling `bson:"module_leveling"`
133		}

136				return nil, nil
137			}
138			return nil, fmt.Errorf("module leveling update (pre-read): %w", err)
139		}
140	
141		// Se mezcla sobre una copia para que la vista del llamador nunca quede a
142		// medio mezclar.
143		merged := before.ModuleLeveling
144		if merged.SchemaVersion == 0 {
145			merged = mocks.NewModuleLeveling()
146		}
147		if err := MergeDeepJSON(&merged, patch); err != nil {
148			return nil, fmt.Errorf("module leveling update (merge): %w", err)
149		}
150		// El `updated_at` PROPIO del módulo se estampa a `now` DESPUÉS de la
151		// mezcla — el body estricto del PATCH rechaza la clave, así que nunca
152		// llega en `patch`.
153		merged.UpdatedAt = dbguild.NewDate(time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond))
154		// Se estampa `schema_version` directo sobre el struct mezclado para no
155		// chocar con el `module_leveling` del mismo `$set`.
156		merged.SchemaVersion = dbguild.SchemaVersionLeveling
157		// Garantiza que las colecciones vacías sigan no-nil ([] / {}) tras la

159		dbguild.NormalizeLeveling(&merged)
160	
161		// `enabled_since` es WRITE-ONCE y EXCLUSIVAMENTE server-side. Se
162		// restaura primero el valor ALMACENADO, pisando lo que la mezcla haya
163		// podido dejar — el body estricto ya rechaza la clave, esto es defensa
164		// en profundidad.
165		merged.EnabledSince = before.ModuleLeveling.EnabledSince
166	
167		// Se estampa la PRIMERA vez que el módulo queda activado y no se

169		if merged.Enabled && merged.EnabledSince == nil {
170			stamp := dbguild.NewDate(time.Now().UTC().Truncate(time.Millisecond))
171			merged.EnabledSince = &stamp
172		}
173	
174		update := bson.M{
175			"$set": bson.M{
176				"module_leveling": merged,
177			},
178			"$currentDate": bson.M{"updatedAt": true},
179		}

181		opt = opt.SetProjection(bson.M{"module_leveling": 1})

188			}

190		}

## Summary

Added a `requirements` block to the leveling module config in `services/api-db-go`, matching the shape already defined in `libraries/library-shared`'s `DBLevelingRequirements`:

- **`internal/domain/dbguild/module_leveling.go`**: new `LevelingRequirements` struct (membership/account-age/message-length minimums, four text-only ignore flags, `bypass_role_ids`), nested as `Requirements` on `LevelingXpSource` (so it lives under both `text` and `voice`). `NormalizeLeveling` now backfills nil `bypass_role_ids` to `[]`.
- **`internal/domain/mocks/module_leveling_mock.go`**: `levelingRequirementsDefault()` (all-zero/false defaults) wired into `NewModuleLeveling`'s `Text`/`Voice`.
- **`internal/domain/validations/module_leveling_validations.go`**: new `ValidateUpdateModuleLeveling` (+ `validateLevelingRequirements` helper) rejecting negative seconds/length and non-snowflake or oversized `bypass_role_ids`, following the existing greeter/TTS validation pattern.
- **`internal/application/handlers/module_leveling_handler.go`**: wired the new validator into `Patch`, same spot as `ValidateUpdateModuleGreeter`.
- **`internal/infrastructure/redis/module_cache.go`**: no code change needed — `MarshalModuleLeveling` already JSON-encodes `text`/`voice` wholesale, so `requirements` is cached automatically; added a doc comment explaining that.
- Tests added: `module_leveling_test.go` (normalize) and `module_leveling_validations_test.go` (validation), following existing conventions. `gofmt` passes on all touched files; no build/tests were run per instructions.
